title: Spotify expands audiobook service to over 180 global markets
summary: Streaming provider Spotify has expanded its audiobook service to more than 180 markets worldwide. The expansion brings a catalog of 350,000 titles across 120 languages to international users.
point1: Spotify expanded audiobooks to over 180 international markets.
point2: The rollout makes 350,000 audiobook titles available across 120 languages.

title: Serum Institute's Cervavac HPV vaccine earns WHO prequalification
summary: The World Health Organization has granted prequalification status to Cervavac, the quadrivalent HPV vaccine manufactured by the Serum Institute of India. Inclusion on the WHO list allows United Nations agencies to purchase and distribute the vaccine internationally for individuals aged 9 to 26.
point1: Serum Institute of India's Cervavac HPV vaccine received formal WHO prequalification status.
point2: The prequalification allows global procurement agencies like UN bodies to buy the vaccine for worldwide immunization.

title: RBI raises repo rate to 5.50% and shifts stance to 'calibrated tightening'
summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, marking its first interest rate hike in nearly three and a half years. The central bank also changed its monetary policy stance from 'neutral' to 'calibrated tightening' amid rising inflation pressures driven by the West Asia conflict.
point1: The RBI Monetary Policy Committee increased the key repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%.
point2: This rate hike is the central bank's first in nearly three and a half years, accompanied by an increased FY27 inflation projection of 5.2%.

title: Indian government intervenes to halt Adani's Mumbai airport slot cuts
summary: The Indian Civil Aviation Ministry has intervened to put proposed international flight slot cuts at Mumbai airport on hold. The cuts had been proposed by Adani, the airport's operator, and the government's intervention aims to allow stakeholders to develop a transition plan.
point1: The Civil Aviation Ministry halted proposed international slot cuts at Mumbai airport.
point2: The intervention prevents immediate disruption to international flight schedules at one of India's busiest hubs.
point3: Stakeholders are currently working to establish a transition plan.

title: World Bank raises India's FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7.1%
summary: The World Bank has upgraded its GDP growth projection for India to 7.1% for the fiscal year 2027. The upward revision is driven by stronger-than-expected export performance, which is anticipated to provide a significant upside to the country's economic outlook.
point1: The World Bank raised India's FY27 GDP growth projection to 7.1%.
point2: Stronger export performance is cited as the primary driver of the improved economic outlook.

title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge under Skydance
summary: Hollywood studios Paramount and Warner Bros are merging to form a single entity under Skydance, led by billionaire David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz. The merger brings together two of America's oldest film production companies.
point1: Paramount and Warner Bros are merging under the Skydance banner.
point2: The deal represents a massive consolidation of power in the global entertainment and film industry.
point3: No confirmed timeline reported for the completion of the merger.

title: Finland halts construction on two Google data centers over environmental concerns
summary: Finland has ordered a temporary halt to construction work on two planned Google data centers. The decision was made following environmental concerns regarding forest clearance at the project sites.
point1: Finnish authorities ordered a work stoppage on two Google data center projects.
point2: The halt underscores the increasing regulatory and environmental scrutiny facing large-scale tech infrastructure in Europe.
point3: No confirmed timeline reported for when construction might resume.

title: Ship sinks in Black Sea following drone attack
summary: A ship has sunk and its crew is missing following a drone attack in the Black Sea. The incident occurs as Russia intensifies its maritime strikes in the region as part of its war against Ukraine.
point1: A vessel sank in the Black Sea after being targeted by a drone.
point2: The attack highlights the growing danger to commercial and military shipping in the Black Sea corridor.
point3: Search and rescue operations are ongoing for the missing crew.

title: Mistral releases new 1-trillion-parameter multimodal AI model
summary: French AI startup Mistral AI has released Mistral Large 4, a new multimodal model featuring one trillion parameters. The open-weight model, also referred to as 'Le Chonk', is designed to compete with frontier models from U.S. and Chinese rivals.
point1: Mistral Large 4 is a trillion-parameter multimodal model released with open weights.
point2: The release is intended to demonstrate that Mistral remains competitive with leading global AI labs.
point3: No confirmed timeline reported for further iterations.

title: AI computing startup Lambda to raise $4B ahead of planned IPO
summary: Nvidia-backed AI computing startup Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation. The funding round is being led by Coatue and Blackstone.
point1: The funding round is aimed at preparing the company for a planned IPO.
point2: This massive capital raise highlights the ongoing surge in valuation for AI infrastructure providers.
point3: The company plans to launch its IPO in 2027.

title: Kenya confirms its first Ebola death as outbreak spreads
summary: Kenya has confirmed its first death from Ebola as the regional outbreak continues to spread. The deceased patient had previously been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where the disease has claimed over 4,000 lives this year.
point1: Kenya recorded its first Ebola death from a patient who had been living in the DR Congo.
point2: The death raises concerns about the cross-border spread of the outbreak, which has killed over 4,000 in DR Congo.

title: OpenAI launches visual ads that appear alongside image generation results
summary: OpenAI is introducing visual advertisements that will appear next to image generation results. The ads will initially roll out in the United States later this month with a select group of test advertisers.
point1: Visual ads will begin appearing alongside image generation results in the U.S.
point2: This marks a significant step in OpenAI's monetization strategy for its generative AI tools.
point3: The ads are scheduled to begin appearing in the U.S. later in October 2026.

title: MoD inks ₹661 crore contract to procure BrahMos fire control system, launchers for Navy ships
summary: India's Ministry of Defence has signed a ₹661 crore contract to procure BrahMos fire control systems and launchers for Indian Navy warships. The BrahMos is the Navy's primary surface-to-surface missile system for maritime strike operations.
point1: The contract is valued at ₹661 crore for fire control systems and launchers.
point2: The procurement strengthens the Indian Navy's primary maritime strike capabilities onboard frontline warships.

title: Indian opposition MPs detained in protest against election chief
summary: Several Indian opposition MPs, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi, were detained during a protest march to the Election Commission of India. The opposition is demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of voter roll manipulation.
point1: Opposition leaders allege that CEC Gyanesh Kumar manipulated voter rolls to favor the ruling party.
point2: High-profile leaders Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi were among those detained during the standoff with police.

title: 11 Indian crew injured after ship hit by projectile in Strait of Hormuz; India condemns attack
summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs has condemned an attack on the Panama-flagged vessel MT On Peace in the Strait of Hormuz. The projectile strike injured 12 crew members, including 11 Indian nationals.
point1: Eleven Indian crew members were among the 12 injured when the MT On Peace was hit by a projectile.
point2: The incident occurred in the highly sensitive Strait of Hormuz, prompting strong condemnation from India.

title: 'Ghost particles' from space telescope wins physics Nobel
summary: Belgian physicist Professor Francis Halzen has won the Nobel Prize in Physics for his pioneering work on an observatory that detects particles from space. The observatory is designed to detect neutrinos, often referred to as 'ghost particles'.
point1: Francis Halzen won the Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on a space telescope detecting neutrinos.
point2: The research helps scientists understand high-energy cosmic phenomena using subatomic particles.

title: Former German spy chief arrested for espionage and treason
summary: Former German intelligence chief August Hanning has been arrested on charges of espionage and treason. He is accused of obtaining classified information for a foreign power.
point1: August Hanning was arrested for allegedly obtaining classified information for a foreign power.
point2: The arrest of a former top intelligence official represents a major national security breach for Germany.

title: SEBI to partly reverse derivative settlement rules after pushback, sources say
summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is reportedly planning to partly reverse its derivative settlement rules following significant pushback. The regulator received approximately 20,000 suggestions in response to a consultation paper released last month.
point1: SEBI is planning to partly reverse its derivative settlement rules.
point2: The decision follows pushback and approximately 20,000 suggestions received on a consultation paper.

title: Centre elevates three Chief Justices to Supreme Court
summary: The Indian government has elevated three High Court Chief Justices to the Supreme Court. With these new appointments, the working strength of the apex court has increased to 37 judges.
point1: The Indian government elevated three High Court Chief Justices to the Supreme Court.
point2: The appointments increase the working strength of the Supreme Court to 37.

title: Spain PM pins hopes on housing crisis to help win snap election
summary: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has called a snap election, aiming to leverage the country's housing crisis to secure a victory. The move is described as a carefully planned political maneuver rather than a knee-jerk reaction.
point1: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap election in Spain.
point2: Sánchez is focusing on the country's housing crisis to build political support.

title: 'Not again': Arrest of US marine for murder reignites protests in Japan's Okinawa
summary: The arrest of a U.S. Marine on suspicion of murder has reignited protests in Okinawa, Japan. The incident has brought long-standing local frustrations regarding the presence of U.S. military bases back to the forefront.
point1: A U.S. Marine was arrested on suspicion of murder in Okinawa, Japan.
point2: The arrest has reignited local protests against the U.S. military presence on the island.

title: Fort Hood shooter to be executed by firing squad, in first since World War Two
summary: Nidal Malik Hasan, the convicted Fort Hood shooter, is set to be executed by a firing squad. This will mark the first U.S. military execution since 1961 and the first by firing squad since the end of World War II.
point1: Nidal Malik Hasan will be executed by a military firing squad.
point2: It is the first military execution since 1961 and the first by firing squad since World War II.

title: Separatist party projected to win Quebec election, adding new test to Canada's unity
summary: The separatist Parti Québécois is projected to win a minority in the Quebec election, presenting a new challenge to Canada's national unity. The party has pledged to hold an independence referendum in the coming years.
point1: The Parti Québécois is projected to win a minority government in Quebec.
point2: The victory introduces a new test to Canada's national unity.
point3: The party has vowed to hold an independence referendum in the years to come.

title: Rural Data Centers Are in for a Big Federal Tax Break
summary: Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, data center projects in rural areas could become eligible for major federal tax benefits starting next year. However, some major hyperscalers do not seem eager to take advantage of the free cash.
point1: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act provides tax breaks for rural data center projects.
point2: The benefits are designed to incentivize infrastructure development in rural areas.
point3: The tax benefits are scheduled to start next year.

title: Supreme Court refuses to stay proceedings against Nicobar project
summary: The Supreme Court of India has refused to stay a Calcutta High Court order regarding the Great Nicobar Island project, declaring the preservation of culture a fundamental right. Petitions argue that diverting over 130 square kilometers of pristine forest violates the Forest Rights Act and threatens indigenous Shompen and Nicobarese communities.
point1: The Supreme Court declined to halt Calcutta High Court proceedings against the Great Nicobar project.
point2: The court emphasized that the preservation of culture is a fundamental right.

title: First international cargo vessel leaves eastern Assam since 1947
summary: The first international cargo vessel has departed from eastern Assam's Dibrugarh port since 1947. The departure marks a significant step in reviving Dibrugarh, once one of India's busiest river ports, for international trade.
point1: An international cargo vessel left Dibrugarh, Assam, for the first time since 1947.
point2: The event is part of efforts to restore Dibrugarh as a major river port for goods movement.

title: Trump says 'threat' led US to pull bombers from RAF Fairford
summary: The Pentagon confirmed it has removed B1 bombers from RAF Fairford in England back to their home stations in the United States. Donald Trump stated that an unspecified 'threat' prompted the relocation.
point1: B1 bombers were pulled from the UK base and returned to the U.S.
point2: Donald Trump attributed the sudden relocation to a 'threat.'

title: Lucid Motors’ EV output falls to lowest level in almost 2 years
summary: Lucid Motors is deliberately limiting its electric vehicle production after years of struggling to find mass-market demand. The company's EV output has fallen to its lowest level in almost two years.
point1: Lucid is intentionally restricting production due to weak demand.
point2: The production volume has hit its lowest point in nearly two years.

title: OpenAI will start watermarking ChatGPT’s text in the EU
summary: OpenAI announced it will begin watermarking ChatGPT and Codex text in the European Union to comply with the EU AI Act. The company noted that editing the text can make these invisible marks harder to detect.
point1: The watermarking is designed to comply with the European Union's AI Act.
point2: It applies to text generated by both ChatGPT and Codex.
